# Attribution audit — Acoustic Ledger

Task 4.1 from `CLAUDE-CODE-TASKS.md`. This is an audit of what the site
actually ships, done to reduce the chance a copyright claim *against* this
site would be valid. It does not, and cannot, prevent someone from filing a
claim regardless of the facts — see the framing note at the top of
`CLAUDE-CODE-TASKS.md`. Dated 2026-09-15.

## Product images — `public/products/*.webp` (12 files)

**Provenance: 100% procedurally generated by this repo's own code. No
third-party image service, no stock photography, no AI image model.**

`scripts/generate-images.ts` builds each image as hand-authored SVG (a paper
background, a fine grid, copper corner brackets, and a per-category "glyph" —
a monitor, a headphone, an EQ slider bank, etc. — assembled from `<rect>`,
`<circle>` and `<path>` primitives with plain arithmetic) and rasterizes it to
`.webp` with `sharp`, a local, open-source image-processing library
(Apache-2.0 / LGPL-3.0-or-later — see the Dependencies section; it runs
entirely at build time and ships no code to the browser). Nothing in the
pipeline calls out to a network image API or a generative model.

The brief this audit responds to expected 13 files; the repository currently
has 12 (`monitor-front-01`, `monitor-angle-02`, `monitor-sub-03`,
`headphone-over-01`, `headphone-compact-02`, `eq-sliders-01`, `eq-knobs-02`,
`amp-meters-01`, `interface-jacks-02`, `cable-xlr-01`, `cable-trs-02`,
`stand-iso-01`), matching the 12 keys in `scripts/generate-images.ts`'s
`IMAGES` map exactly — there is no 13th image or generator entry to account
for. Not a finding, just a correction to the brief's count.

**Verdict: clear. Nothing to replace.**

## Fonts — `src/app/layout.tsx` (`next/font/google`)

| Family | License | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| Saira | SIL Open Font License 1.1 | `OFL.txt` present at `google/fonts` GitHub repo, `ofl/saira/` |
| Saira Condensed | SIL Open Font License 1.1 | `OFL.txt` present at `ofl/sairacondensed/` |
| JetBrains Mono | SIL Open Font License 1.1 | `OFL.txt` present at `ofl/jetbrainsmono/` |

All three live under Google Fonts' `ofl/` directory (checked directly against
the `google/fonts` repository rather than assumed), which is exactly the
license family Google Fonts uses for fonts cleared for free commercial use,
embedding, and self-hosting. OFL's only real restriction — don't sell the
font software itself under the original name, rename true derivatives — does
not apply to using these fonts in a storefront's UI.

`next/font/google` downloads the font files at build time and serves them
from this site's own origin (no runtime request to Google, no
render-blocking third-party font request either) — self-hosting is
explicitly permitted by OFL and is exactly what the license anticipates for
embedding a font in a product.

**Verdict: clear.**

## Seed data — `src/db/seed.ts` (5 categories, 38 products, 66 variants)

Read in full. Every product line name is an invented, generic/descriptive
word or phrase — *Datum, Reference, Fieldglass, Baseline, Calibrate,
Parametric, Graphic, Contour, Headroom, Current, Interface, Line, Ledger* —
combined with plain size/spec numbers ("Datum 5 Nearfield Monitor", "Current
100 Power Amplifier"). None of them, individually or as the storefront's own
brand name "Acoustic Ledger", match or nearly match a real audio-equipment
manufacturer or product line (checked by name against the major studio-monitor
/ headphone / interface makers: Yamaha, JBL, Genelec, Focal, Neumann, KRK,
Adam Audio, Mackie, PreSonus, RME, Focusrite, Universal Audio, API, SSL,
Neve, Warm Audio, Behringer, Shure, Sennheiser, Audio-Technica, Beyerdynamic,
Avid). The two seeded people ("Store Admin", "Alex Rivera") are generic demo
names, not real people.

No pricing, review, or press content anywhere in the seed data is presented
as real — it's plainly a fictional demo catalog throughout, consistent with
`PRODUCT.md`'s existing evidence-absence list (no reviews, press, benchmarks,
or company story anywhere in the site).

**Verdict: clear.**

## Dependencies (`npx license-checker --summary`, 645 packages)

```
MIT: 548        ISC: 31         Apache-2.0: 31    BSD-2-Clause: 12
BSD-3-Clause: 9  MPL-2.0: 5      BlueOak-1.0.0: 2  Python-2.0: 1
CC-BY-4.0: 1     CC0-1.0: 1      UNLICENSED: 1     0BSD: 1
Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later: 1
```

Everything outside the top four (MIT/ISC/Apache-2.0/BSD) individually
identified and checked — none require action:

| Package | License | Why it's fine |
|---|---|---|
| `@img/sharp-win32-x64` (sharp's native binding) | Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later | Build-time only (image generation, Next's image optimizer) — never shipped to the browser. LGPL's obligations attach to distributing the library itself, satisfied by normal dynamic-linking npm usage; nothing here modifies or statically embeds the LGPL code into the app's own source. |
| `axe-core` (via `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`, via `eslint-config-next`) | MPL-2.0 | Lint-time only — confirmed with `npm ls axe-core`, it's a transitive devDependency of ESLint's accessibility plugin, never bundled into the app. MPL is file-level copyleft on its own unmodified files; not a concern for an unmodified, dev-only dependency. |
| `lightningcss` (x2 versions) | MPL-2.0 | Tailwind's CSS build tool — same reasoning as axe-core: build-time, unmodified. |
| `argparse` | Python-2.0 | A CLI-argument-parsing library ported from Python's stdlib `argparse`; the license classifier picked up its historical Python-2.0 lineage. Permissive in practice (also carries an MIT-equivalent grant); build-tooling transitive dependency, not shipped code. |
| `caniuse-lite` (via Browserslist) | CC-BY-4.0 | A browser-compatibility data table used by the build toolchain (Tailwind/PostCSS/Autoprefixer), not code or content in the shipped app. |
| `language-subtag-registry` | CC0-1.0 | Public domain data table (IANA language subtag registry), used by a transitive dependency. No restriction at all. |
| `store@0.1.0` (this project) | UNLICENSED | That's just this repo's own unset `license` field in `package.json` — not a third-party dependency. Fixed by Task 4.2's `LICENSE` file and `package.json` update. |

No GPL, AGPL, or SSPL anywhere in the dependency tree — nothing here creates
an obligation to release this project's own source code.

**Verdict: clear.**

## UI components — `src/components/ui/` (shadcn "base-nova" over Base UI)

- **Base UI** (`@base-ui/react`, `@base-ui/utils`) — npm dependency, **MIT**
  (confirmed in the dependency table above).
- **shadcn/ui** — not an npm dependency; its CLI copies component source
  directly into `src/components/ui/`, which is why those files are editable
  project code rather than a `node_modules` package. shadcn/ui's own license
  (MIT) explicitly permits this: copying, modifying, and shipping the
  generated components in any project, commercial or not, with no required
  attribution in the shipped product.

**Verdict: clear.**

## Summary

Every category audited comes back clear: no stock imagery, no unverified
font licensing, no real-brand collisions in the fictional catalog, no
copyleft dependency that reaches the shipped app, and both UI foundations
(Base UI, shadcn/ui) are MIT. There is nothing in this list that needs
replacing.

This is not legal advice, and confirming *this* audit found nothing does not
mean a claim against this site is impossible — see Task 4.4 on making
copying provable, and the general framing note that no code change makes a
copyright claim unfileable.
